typography/clamp-text.a11y:
The switch is a real button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the text; the whole text stays in the
document while folded (screen readers read all of it). The fold is measured after layout and when the box resizes, so
a text that fits never shows a switch.

typography/code-view.notes:
```tsx
<CodeView code={source} lang="tsx" langLabel="Counter.tsx" wrapLabel="Soft wrap" copyLabel="Copy code" />
<CodeView code={snippet} lang="sh" toolbar={false} lineNumbers={false} />
```
typography/code-view.a11y:
The code area is focusable (`tabindex=0`) so it scrolls from the keyboard; line numbers are `aria-hidden`, so copying or
reading gives only the code. The Wrap button reports its state with `aria-pressed`. Colours are theme text tokens and
stay readable in every theme.

props: plain key text when `keys` is not given
typography/kbd.a11y: A real `<kbd>` element: screen readers announce it as keyboard input.

typography/overflow-text.notes:
```tsx
<Marquee text={news} separator={<Icon of={star} />} />
<OverflowText text={title} easing="linear" disabled={() => !prefs.motion} />
<Marquee duplicate separator={false} pause={0}>{logos.map((l) => <Logo {...l} />)}</Marquee>
```

With `duplicate` a short content (a row of logos, a few quotes) still fills the box and loops: the content is a
`.m-marquee-unit` and its copies follow it (space them with a gap and an end padding on that class). The copies are
`aria-hidden` and `inert`, so links and buttons in them are neither read nor focused.
typography/overflow-text.a11y:
`dir="auto"` so mixed scripts read correctly; one readable copy (loop and `duplicate` copies are `aria-hidden` and inert); no movement under
reduced motion; the motion engine's global speed and "stop all" apply.

typography/section-label.a11y:
Choose the element with `as`: a heading level where the label starts a section of the page, `legend` in a
`<fieldset>`, `li` + `role="presentation"` inside a listbox, plain `div` when a group is named through
`aria-labelledby` (give the label an `id`). Uppercase is a CSS transform only: screen readers read the text as written.
The icon is decorative.
